summary: The maintained Python package commits all grpc_tools.protoc outputs and its dev extra pins the generator. Generated gRPC and protobuf guards define runtime minimums; broad test/build ranges remain broad when clean installs admit the intended stable versions. Regenerating the complete existing proto catalog can expose previously stale coordinator/state and missing live_control output without changing schema. The .NET client stays net8.0, generates C# through the build-only Grpc.Tools reference, and was exercised against a Python gRPC fixture on TCP and UDS. Such transport controls do not qualify native engine behavior, installed fleet adoption or the engine-event latency budget. Retrieve current manifests and feeds before future refreshes; the cited qualification is historical evidence, not current package selection authority.
title: Python committed generators and runtime floors move together
